4.title: Scope of Services, Products and Deliverables
4.counselNotes: Use the high-level scope only for low-value, low-risk, non-critical engagements (for example, contract value below [USD 10,000], non-regulated, no customer data, no production systems, established vendor). Do not use it for regulated, customer-facing, data-processing, security-sensitive or production-critical services — use the Baseline or Buy-Side scope instead.

1.title: Recitals and Background
1.baseline:
Recitals.
(A) [Describe each Party and its business or role relevant to this transaction.]
(B) [Describe the commercial background: why the Parties are entering into this relationship, and the business problem or opportunity being addressed.]
(C) [Describe what each Party will do under this Agreement: the Company will [provide / procure / license], and the Counterparty will [provide / procure / license].]
(D) [State any relevant factual assumptions, regulatory context or prior dealings between the Parties that provide necessary context.]
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants in this Agreement and for other good and valuable consideration (the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged), the Parties agree as set out below.
1.counselNotes: Recitals are drafted jointly with Business, which provides the factual background and commercial rationale. Recitals must not contain operative obligations, service commitments, performance standards, guaranteed volumes or regulatory-status representations — those belong in the operative clauses. Keep recitals factual and non-binding.

2.title: Definitions and Interpretation
2.fallback: Definitions in a Schedule. Defined terms may be set out in a Schedule rather than in a consolidated Definitions clause, provided that: (a) Clause [●] (Order of Precedence) states that Schedules form part of this Agreement and prevail over the main body in the event of inconsistency; (b) the definitions Schedule is version-locked at execution (dated, initialled by both Parties and incorporated by reference); and (c) defined terms are capitalised consistently throughout, and the Schedule is the sole source of those definitions.

3.title: Contract Structure and Order of Precedence
3.baseline:
Contract Structure and Order of Precedence.
(a) This Agreement comprises: (i) the main body (including the Recitals and all operative clauses); (ii) all Schedules, Annexes and Exhibits expressly forming part of this Agreement; (iii) any Data Processing Addendum or Information Security Schedule; (iv) any Statement of Work, Order Form or Purchase Order executed under this Agreement; and (v) any documents expressly incorporated by reference and version-locked at the Effective Date.
(b) If there is any conflict or inconsistency, the following order of precedence applies (highest first): (i) any written amendment executed by both Parties under Clause [●] (Amendment); (ii) the main body of this Agreement; (iii) the Data Processing Addendum or Information Security Schedule (for data-protection, security or privacy matters); (iv) any Statement of Work or Order Form (for the specific services, deliverables, timelines or fees in that document); (v) all other Schedules, Annexes and Exhibits; and (vi) any other documents incorporated by reference.
(c) No terms in any online terms of service, general terms of business or pre-printed terms of the Counterparty form part of, or vary, this Agreement unless expressly incorporated in writing by an authorised representative of the Company under Clause [●] (Amendment).
3.buyside:
Enhanced Precedence Protections. In addition to the Baseline order of precedence:
(a) the Company's policies and standards expressly incorporated by reference (including its Information Security Policy and Data Protection Policy) rank equally with the Data Processing Addendum for matters within their scope;
(b) the Counterparty's standard or pre-printed terms have no effect unless attached as a Schedule, expressly identified as incorporated, approved in writing by the Company, and version-locked at the Effective Date; and
(c) any document incorporated by reference is effective only as at the version in force on the Effective Date, and the Counterparty may not unilaterally update it in any way that expands the Company's obligations or reduces its rights or protections.
3.sellside: Supplier-Side Precedence. Where the Company is the supplier, this Agreement prevails over the Counterparty's order forms for all matters other than the pricing, volume and service parameters expressly stated in the order form, and the Company's product terms and acceptable-use and security policies prevail for use of the Platform.
3.fallback: Incorporation by Reference. A document may be incorporated by reference (by URL or citation) rather than attached, provided that: (a) it is available at a permanent, non-editable location stated in writing at execution; (b) it is version-locked by date, version number or checksum; (c) it has been approved by the Company before execution; (d) the Counterparty may not unilaterally update it without the Company's prior written consent; and (e) the Company retains a copy as at the Effective Date. Incorporation of a document "as updated from time to time", or by reference to its "current version", is not acceptable.

6.title: Conditions Precedent
6.baseline:
Conditions Precedent.
(a) Neither Party is required to commence performance unless and until all conditions precedent in Schedule [●] (Conditions Precedent) have been satisfied or expressly waived in writing by the Party entitled to their benefit. Each condition is for the benefit of the Party identified in Schedule [●], and only that Party may waive it.
(b) The Party responsible for a condition shall use commercially reasonable efforts to satisfy it by the date specified in Schedule [●] and shall provide the beneficiary with written evidence of satisfaction. No condition is satisfied by conduct, commencement of performance or passage of time; satisfaction must be confirmed in writing by the beneficiary.
(c) If any condition is not satisfied or waived by [●] (the Longstop Date), either Party may terminate this Agreement by written notice, whereupon: (i) neither Party has any further obligation to the other; (ii) any fees, deposits or advance payments are refunded in full within [thirty (30)] days; and (iii) neither Party is liable to the other for the termination, save for obligations accrued before termination.
6.fallback: Light-Touch Conditions (Low-Risk Engagements). For low-value, low-risk engagements with established counterparties, the conditions precedent may be limited to: (a) execution by both Parties of all contract documents; and (b) receipt by the supplier of any upfront payment or deposit.
6.counselNotes: Use light-touch conditions only for low-value, low-risk, routine engagements with no customer data, no production systems and no regulated activities. Where the arrangement involves production integrations, customer data, regulated activities, custody of Customer Assets or security-sensitive systems, retain and satisfy the full Buy-Side conditions precedent before performance commences.

5.title: Term, Renewal, Extension and Expiry

variants.label: Model 1 — Indefinite Term
variants.whenToUse: Ongoing operational relationships where either Party needs flexibility to exit without a fixed commitment period (e.g. platform partnerships, distribution arrangements, non-exclusive licences, operational services where business needs may change).
variants.text: 5.1 This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues in full force and effect unless and until terminated by either Party in accordance with Clause [●] (Termination). Either Party may terminate this Agreement for convenience (without cause) by giving the other Party not less than [sixty (60)] days' prior written notice, without penalty or liability except for obligations accrued prior to the effective date of termination.

variants.label: Model 2 — Controlled Automatic Renewal
variants.whenToUse: Routine services where continuity is commercially desirable but the exit option must be preserved (e.g. SaaS subscriptions, support and maintenance, non-critical infrastructure). Note: where this Agreement governs critical services, regulated services, data processing, custody, payment processing or core infrastructure, the non-renewal notice period shall be not less than ninety (90) days to allow adequate transition planning, data migration and service cutover.
variants.text:
5.2 This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for an initial period of [●] [months / years] (the Initial Term). Upon expiry of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive renewal periods of [●] [months / years] (each, a Renewal Term), unless either Party gives the other written notice of non-renewal not less than [thirty (30)] days prior to the end of the then-current term (whether Initial Term or Renewal Term). Any such notice shall be effective as of the last day of the then-current term, and this Agreement shall terminate automatically on that date without further action by either Party.
5.3 Unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties: (a) pricing, fees and charges for any Renewal Term shall be as stated in this Agreement or, if no pricing is stated for Renewal Terms, the same as for the immediately preceding term; (b) the Counterparty may propose pricing adjustments for any Renewal Term by giving the Company written notice not less than [sixty (60)] days prior to commencement of that Renewal Term, and any such adjustment requires the Company's written acceptance; and (c) all other terms and conditions remain unchanged unless the Parties expressly agree otherwise in writing.

variants.label: Model 3 — Defined Term with Company Renewal Option
variants.whenToUse: Strategic relationships where the Company wishes to control whether to continue (e.g. key vendor relationships, technology partnerships, or services where the Company has negotiated favourable terms and wants a unilateral right to extend). Gives the Company continuation optionality without obligating it to renew.
variants.text:
5.4 This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for a period of [●] [months / years] (the Initial Term), unless terminated earlier in accordance with Clause [●] (Termination). Upon expiry of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically terminate unless the Company exercises its renewal option in accordance with this Clause.
5.5 The Company shall have the option to renew this Agreement for one or more additional renewal periods of [●] [months / years] (each, a Renewal Term) by giving the Counterparty written notice of renewal not less than [thirty (30)] days prior to expiry of the then-current term. The Company's election to renew or not renew shall be in its sole discretion, and the Company shall have no obligation to provide any reason or justification.
5.6 Unless the Parties agree otherwise in writing: (a) each Renewal Term shall be on the same terms and conditions as the Initial Term (or the immediately preceding Renewal Term); (b) pricing for each Renewal Term shall not exceed pricing for the immediately preceding term unless the Company expressly agrees a pricing adjustment in writing; and (c) the Counterparty shall not impose, introduce or reinstate any minimum volume commitments, exclusivity obligations, non-compete restrictions or similar limitations not present in the Initial Term without the Company's express written consent.
5.7 The Counterparty acknowledges that the Company's decision to renew or not renew is the Company's business decision, and the Counterparty shall have no right to compel renewal, claim damages for non-renewal, or seek injunctive or other equitable relief to prevent expiry. The Counterparty shall plan its operations and resource allocation on the assumption that the Company may elect not to renew.

variants.label: Model 4 — Defined Term with Mutual Agreement to Extend
variants.whenToUse: Project-based arrangements, pilots, proofs of concept, high-risk or novel arrangements, regulated services requiring affirmative compliance sign-off, or arrangements where both Parties must reassess and recommit at the end of the term (e.g. custody arrangements, joint ventures, partnerships requiring Board approval).
variants.text:
5.8 This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for a period of [●] [months / years] (the Term), unless terminated earlier in accordance with Clause [●] (Termination). Upon expiry of the Term, this Agreement shall automatically terminate and cease to have any further force or effect.
5.9 The Parties expressly agree that: (a) this Agreement shall not automatically renew, extend or continue beyond the Term under any circumstances; (b) any extension or renewal shall require a new written agreement executed by duly authorised representatives of both Parties; (c) continued performance, provision of the Services or use of the Platform after expiry of the Term shall not constitute renewal, extension or waiver of this Clause but shall be governed by such interim arrangements as the Parties may expressly agree in writing; and (d) either Party may refuse to enter into a renewal or extension without cause, liability or penalty.
5.10 If either Party wishes to explore renewal or extension beyond the Term, it shall notify the other in writing not less than [ninety (90)] days prior to expiry of the Term. The Parties shall thereafter negotiate in good faith whether to renew or extend and, if so, on what terms, scope, pricing and duration. No renewal or extension shall bind either Party unless and until the Parties execute a written renewal agreement.
5.11 Each Party acknowledges that: (a) neither Party has any obligation to renew or extend this Agreement beyond the Term; (b) either Party may decline to renew or extend for any reason or no reason, in its sole discretion, without liability or penalty; and (c) the other Party shall have no right to claim damages, loss of profits, reliance damages, expectation damages or any other compensation arising from non-renewal or non-extension.

5.redflags:
Automatic renewal (Model 2) with a notice period shorter than fourteen (14) days for routine services or ninety (90) days for critical services, preventing adequate transition planning and vendor sourcing.
Automatic renewal that introduces, imposes or reinstates minimum volume commitments, exclusivity obligations, non-compete restrictions, pricing increases or penalty clauses not present in the Initial Term, locking the Company into unfavourable terms.
Multi-year Initial Term (greater than 24 months) without: (i) a termination-for-convenience right after [12] months; (ii) pricing protection (fixed or CPI-capped); or (iii) performance conditions allowing termination for sustained non-performance.
Indefinite term (Model 1) without a termination-for-convenience right, or with a termination notice period exceeding sixty (60) days, creating indefinite lock-in.
Company renewal option (Model 3) exercisable only if the Counterparty meets performance conditions, effectively giving the Counterparty a veto over the Company's renewal right.
Fixed term with mutual agreement (Model 4) combined with minimum volume commitments or take-or-pay obligations extending beyond the Term, creating financial exposure after expiry.
5.usageNotes:
Select term model based on: (i) service criticality (critical services should not use indefinite term or short-notice automatic renewal); (ii) strategic importance (strategic relationships where [Company] wants control use Model 3 - [Company] renewal option); (iii) vendor dependency risk (high dependency use Model 4 - mutual agreement, requiring affirmative recommitment); (iv) transition complexity (complex transitions require longer notice periods).
For critical technology, regulated services, data processing, custody or infrastructure: avoid automatic renewal (Model 2) unless notice period is [ninety (90)] days minimum and termination for convenience right exists; prefer Model 3 ([Company] renewal option) or Model 4 (mutual agreement) requiring affirmative decision and adequate transition planning time.
For routine services (SaaS, office supplies, non-production tools): Model 2 (controlled automatic renewal) with [thirty (30)] days notice is acceptable.
For strategic partnerships or novel arrangements: use Model 4 (mutual agreement) requiring both Parties to recommit, preventing lock-in to arrangements that may not meet evolving business needs.
Maintain renewal calendar for all contracts: diarize Initial Term expiry, notice deadline (if Model 2 or 3), and renewal review trigger date ([120] days before expiry for critical services, [60] days for routine services). For contracts with automatic renewal (Model 2), set calendar reminder [30] days before notice deadline; missed deadline locks [Company] into another term. For contracts with [Company] renewal option (Model 3), Business initiates renewal discussion with Legal [90] days before expiry to confirm whether to exercise option; if exercising option, document decision and send renewal notice before deadline. For contracts requiring mutual agreement (Model 4), Business initiates renewal discussion [120] days before expiry to allow time for renegotiation if both Parties wish to continue.
If counterparty proposes automatic renewal for critical services, negotiate for: (i) [ninety (90)] days notice period; (ii) termination for convenience right exercisable on [ninety (90)] days notice during any Renewal Term; (iii) pricing cap (CPI + [2-3]%) or requirement for [Company] written approval of increases.
Run term audit before signature: (i) identify which model is used; (ii) confirm notice period adequate for service criticality; (iii) confirm pricing protection if automatic renewal or multi-year term; (iv) diarize expiry and notice deadline; (v) assign business owner for renewal decision.
Default rule: for regulated services, customer assets, personal data or critical infrastructure, reject automatic renewal (Model 2) unless [ninety (90)] days notice and termination for convenience right; prefer Model 3 or 4 requiring affirmative renewal decision by Business Approver and Head of Compliance sign-off.

7.title: Onboarding, Implementation, Transition and Go-Live
7.baseline:
Onboarding, Implementation and Go-Live.
(a) Implementation Plan. Each Party shall perform its implementation obligations strictly in accordance with the implementation plan approved in writing by the Company (the Implementation Plan), which shall specify: (i) milestones, deliverables and deadlines; (ii) each Party's responsibilities; (iii) dependencies and prerequisites; (iv) acceptance criteria and testing procedures; (v) go-live criteria and the approval process; and (vi) rollback procedures. Neither Party shall deviate from the Implementation Plan without the Company's prior written approval.
(b) Go-live conditions. Go-live, production deployment or service activation shall not occur unless and until the Company confirms in writing (by email from its authorised representative) that each of the following has been satisfied to its reasonable satisfaction: (i) all conditions precedent in Clause [●] (Conditions Precedent) have been satisfied and documented; (ii) acceptance testing has been completed in accordance with Schedule [●] and the Company has given written acceptance; (iii) all required internal approvals have been obtained (including Compliance for regulated services, Security for production integrations or data access, and Product for customer-facing features); (iv) all defects identified in testing have been remediated to the Company's reasonable satisfaction, or accepted by the Company in writing as known issues with documented workarounds; and (v) rollback, incident-response and support-escalation procedures have been documented, tested and approved.
(c) No deemed acceptance. There shall be no deemed or implied acceptance, and no acceptance by conduct. Acceptance of any Service, Deliverable, milestone or component occurs only on the Company's express written acceptance.
7.counselNotes: Deemed acceptance is not acceptable for production integrations, security-sensitive systems, regulated services, or anything affecting customer data or Customer Assets — require the Company's express written acceptance for those.

8.title: Fees, Payment, Invoicing, Taxes and Set-Off
8.baseline:
Fees and Payment.
(a) Fees. The Company shall pay the Counterparty the fees set out in Schedule [●] (Fees) (the Fees). Unless that Schedule states otherwise, the Fees: (i) are inclusive of all costs, expenses, disbursements, overhead, materials, personnel and travel incurred by the Counterparty in performing this Agreement; (ii) are stated and payable in [currency]; (iii) are exclusive of value-added tax, goods and services tax or equivalent indirect taxes (VAT), which the Company shall pay in addition where applicable; and (iv) shall not be increased or varied without the Company's prior written approval.
(b) Payment terms. The Company shall pay undisputed Fees that are correctly invoiced within [thirty (30)] days of receipt of a correct and compliant invoice. The Company may withhold, set off or dispute any amount in good faith in accordance with Clause [●] (Disputes) and Clause [●] (Set-Off).
(c) Invoicing. Each invoice shall: (i) be addressed to the Company at the address in Schedule [●]; (ii) state the Counterparty's legal name, registered address, tax identification number and bank details; (iii) reference this Agreement; (iv) itemise all Fees and expenses in sufficient detail for the Company to verify them; (v) reference the applicable Statement of Work or Order Form; (vi) include the VAT/GST breakdown and registration numbers where applicable; and (vii) include all information required by Applicable Law for a valid tax invoice. The Company may reject and return any non-compliant invoice, and the payment period shall not start until a corrected invoice is received.
8.buyside:
Enhanced Payment Protections. In addition to the Baseline:
(a) No fee increases. The Counterparty shall not increase or vary any Fee, rate or charge without the Company's express prior written approval; any purported increase without such approval is void.
(b) Payment conditional on acceptance. The Company's obligation to pay any Fee for a Deliverable, milestone or phase is conditional on (i) delivery; (ii) the Company's written acceptance under Clause [●] (Acceptance); and (iii) the Counterparty's compliance with the applicable requirements, specifications and Service Levels. The Company is not obliged to pay for anything it has not accepted in writing.
(c) Audit. On reasonable prior written notice, the Company may audit the Counterparty's billing, time and expense records relating to the Fees. The Counterparty shall keep complete and accurate records for [●] years after each calendar year and make them available during normal business hours. If an audit discloses an overcharge, the Counterparty shall refund it, and if the overcharge exceeds [●]% the Counterparty shall bear the reasonable cost of the audit.
8.sellside:
Payment to the Company.
(a) Due date. The Counterparty shall pay all Fees within [●] days of the invoice date. Time is of the essence for payment. The Company may charge interest on overdue undisputed amounts at [●]% per annum (or the maximum permitted by Applicable Law, if higher) from the due date until payment, compounding monthly.
(b) No set-off. The Counterparty shall pay all amounts in full without set-off, deduction, withholding or counterclaim, except (i) amounts the Company has authorised in writing, or (ii) withholding tax required by law, in which case the Counterparty shall give the Company not less than [thirty (30)] days' prior written notice, deduct only the minimum required, remit it within the time required by law, and promptly provide an official withholding-tax certificate.
(c) Suspension. If the Counterparty fails to pay any undisputed amount by the due date, the Company may (without limiting its other remedies), on [●] days' written notice, suspend the Services, Platform access or delivery of Deliverables, charge a late-payment fee, and require future Fees to be paid in advance.
8.counselNotes: Use advance payment only for low-value, low-risk contracts (for example, value below [USD 50,000]) with a financially sound counterparty. Not acceptable for production integrations, regulated services, customer data, Customer Assets or security-sensitive systems.

9.title: Service Levels, KPIs and Service Credits
9.baseline:
Service Levels and Service Credits.
(a) The Counterparty shall meet the Service Levels set out in Schedule [●] (SLA).
(b) Where the Counterparty fails to meet a Service Level, it shall provide the Company with the service credits calculated under Schedule [●] (SLA).
(c) Service credits are without prejudice to the Company's rights to damages, specific performance, termination and all other remedies, unless this Agreement expressly states that service credits are the sole remedy for a specific, narrowly defined service failure.
(d) The Counterparty shall provide the Company with monthly SLA performance reports and shall immediately notify the Company of any material or imminent failure.
9.sellside: Service Credits as Sole Financial Remedy. Service credits are the Company's sole financial remedy for availability failures that do not: (a) constitute fraud, wilful misconduct or gross negligence by the Company; (b) result in a Data Breach, security incident or loss of Customer Assets; (c) trigger any regulatory breach or mandatory notification obligation; or (d) cause loss exceeding the aggregate service credits payable in the relevant period. Service credits do not limit the Company's termination rights or indemnity claims.
9.fallback: Service Credits as Sole Remedy (Limited). Service credits are the Company's sole and exclusive remedy for the specific, narrowly defined Service Level metrics identified in Schedule [●] (SLA), save that this limitation does not apply to, and the Company retains all remedies for, a Data Breach, a security or regulatory incident, loss of Customer Assets, or wilful misconduct, and does not limit the Company's right to terminate for chronic or critical failure.
9.counselNotes: Agree service credits as sole remedy only where it is confined to specific, non-critical SLA metrics, the carve-outs above are expressly preserved, and the Company keeps its termination rights for chronic or critical failures.

10.title: Performance Standards
10.baseline: Performance Standards. The Counterparty shall perform its obligations under this Agreement with due skill, care and diligence, using appropriately qualified and experienced personnel, and in accordance with: (a) good industry practice for services of the type provided; (b) Applicable Law and Regulatory Requirements; and (c) the standards set out in this Agreement and any applicable Schedule.
10.buyside: Heightened Performance Standard. The Counterparty shall perform all Services to the highest professional standards applicable to services of this type. For services involving regulated activities, data, security, Customer Assets, payment infrastructure or critical operations, the standard of care shall be that of a specialist provider in the relevant field operating in compliance with applicable financial-services, data-protection and cybersecurity requirements. The Counterparty shall promptly replace, at the Company's request, any personnel whose performance does not meet the required standard.
10.sellside: Company Performance Standard. The Company's obligations are limited to reasonable skill and care appropriate to its role as [platform provider / data licensor / technology vendor], and are subject to the dependencies and assumptions set out in Schedule [●]. The Company does not accept liability for outcomes dependent on the Counterparty's own systems, decisions or third-party services.
10.fallback: Reasonable Skill and Care (Low-Risk). The Counterparty shall perform the Services with reasonable skill and care and in accordance with Applicable Law.
10.counselNotes: Use the reasonable skill-and-care standard only for low-risk support or advisory services; for regulated, security-sensitive or critical services use the Baseline or Buy-Side standard.

11.title: Compliance with Laws
11.baseline: Compliance with Laws. Each Party shall comply with all Applicable Law that applies to it and its performance under this Agreement. The Counterparty is solely responsible for compliance with all laws, regulations, orders and regulatory requirements applicable to its business, personnel, systems, services, licences and subcontractors, and shall not take any action that causes the Company to breach Applicable Law.
11.sellside: Company Compliance Limitation. The Company's compliance obligations under this Agreement are limited to those applicable to it in its capacity as [platform provider / data licensor] under this Agreement. The Company is not responsible for ensuring the Counterparty's compliance with laws applicable to the Counterparty's own business, operations or personnel.
11.counselNotes: Accept mutual compliance wording only if each Party's obligations are separately stated and the Company's responsibility is limited to the laws applicable to it in its role under this Agreement.

12.title: Regulatory Compliance and Cooperation
12.baseline:
Regulatory Compliance and Cooperation. The Counterparty shall:
(a) cooperate with the Company and any Regulator in relation to any inquiry, audit, inspection, investigation, reporting obligation or request connected with this Agreement, the Services, Personal Data, Customer Assets or Regulatory Requirements;
(b) provide any information, documentation, records, access or assistance required by the Company to comply with Regulatory Requirements within [five (5)] Business Days of request (or any shorter period required by law); and
(c) immediately notify the Company if it receives any regulatory inquiry, investigation, audit request or enforcement action related to this Agreement or the Services.
12.sellside: Company Cooperation Limitation. The Company's cooperation with the Counterparty's regulators is limited to legally required assistance and shall not require the Company to disclose information protected by legal privilege or confidential to its customers. Requests for extraordinary regulatory assistance beyond routine cooperation shall be at the Counterparty's cost.
12.counselNotes: Accept cooperation obligations subject to confidentiality and legal privilege, provided no restriction applies to cooperation with the Company's own Regulators and the obligation cannot be used to block or delay Regulator access.

13.title: Licensing, Permits and No Regulated Activity Representation
13.baseline:
Licensing, Permits and No Regulated-Activity Representation.
(a) Each Party shall obtain and maintain all licences, approvals, registrations, permits and authorisations required for its business and for its performance under this Agreement. The Counterparty represents and warrants that it holds all licences required to provide the Services and shall promptly notify the Company if any required licence is suspended, revoked, restricted, under investigation or not renewed.
(b) Nothing in this Agreement authorises the Counterparty to conduct regulated activity on behalf of the Company or to hold the Company out as the licensed party in respect of any activity carried out by the Counterparty.
13.buyside:
Enhanced Licensing Obligations. In addition to the Baseline:
(a) the Counterparty shall provide the Company with copies of all required licences and authorisations before commencement of the Services;
(b) the Counterparty shall maintain the required licences in good standing throughout the Term and shall give the Company at least [thirty (30)] days' written notice of any renewal, variation, surrender or revocation; and
(c) if the Counterparty's licence is suspended, revoked or subject to enforcement action, the Company may terminate immediately for regulatory reason under Clause [●] (Termination for Regulatory Reason).
13.sellside: No Company Regulated Service. The Company does not provide investment advice, legal advice, financial planning, tax advice, payment services, custody services, brokerage, dealing or any other regulated service unless expressly stated and licensed by the Company under this Agreement. The Counterparty shall not represent the Company as providing any regulated service that the Company is not expressly licensed to provide.
13.fallback: Licensing (Low-Risk Vendor). The Counterparty represents and warrants that it holds all licences required by law for its business and for its performance under this Agreement.
13.counselNotes: Use the short licensing representation only for low-risk, non-regulated vendor relationships; for regulated or licence-dependent services use the Baseline or Buy-Side licensing provisions.

14.title: Anti-Bribery, AML/CFT, Sanctions, Fraud and Financial Crime
14.baseline:
Anti-Bribery, AML/CFT, Sanctions and Financial Crime.
(a) Each Party shall comply with all applicable anti-bribery, anti-corruption, AML/CFT, counter-terrorist-financing, sanctions, fraud-prevention, market-abuse and financial-crime laws, including the UK Bribery Act 2010, the US Foreign Corrupt Practices Act 1977 and applicable FATF standards.
(b) The Counterparty shall: (i) not take any action that causes the Company to breach those requirements; (ii) maintain adequate procedures and controls to prevent bribery, corruption, money laundering and sanctions violations in connection with this Agreement; and (iii) immediately notify the Company of any actual or suspected financial crime, sanctions issue, AML/CFT concern or regulatory inquiry related to this Agreement or its business.
14.sellside: Company Financial-Crime Limitation. The Company's financial-crime compliance obligations are limited to those applicable to its own licensed business. The Company may suspend or terminate this Agreement immediately if it determines, in its reasonable judgement, that continuation creates financial-crime, sanctions, AML/CFT or reputational risk.
14.counselNotes: Accept mutual compliance with immediate termination on breach (without full audit rights) only for low-risk, non-financial-services contracts; for higher-risk or financial-services contracts use the Buy-Side screening and audit obligations.

15.title: Consumer Protection and Fair Dealing
15.baseline:
Consumer Protection and Fair Dealing. Where the Counterparty communicates with, acts on behalf of, or affects End Users in connection with this Agreement, the Counterparty shall:
(a) ensure that all statements, materials, processes and conduct affecting End Users are accurate, clear, fair, not misleading and compliant with Applicable Law and the Company's approved scripts or materials;
(b) not make any representation, commitment or product claim on behalf of the Company that is not expressly authorised in writing by the Company; and
(c) use only Company-approved materials for any customer-facing or marketing communications.
15.sellside: Counterparty Representations to Customers. The Counterparty shall not: (a) misrepresent the Company's products, fees, risks, licences, regulatory status or capabilities; or (b) make representations about the Company's products to customers without using Company-approved materials. The Counterparty shall immediately take down or correct any inaccurate or unapproved materials on the Company's request.
15.fallback: No Public Statements (Non-Customer-Facing). The Counterparty shall not make any public statement or representation about the Company or its products without the Company's prior written approval.
15.counselNotes: Use the short no-public-statements provision only for non-customer-facing, non-regulated vendor contracts; for customer-facing or regulated arrangements use the Baseline or Buy-Side consumer-protection obligations.

16.title: Data Protection and Personal Data Processing
16.baseline:
Data Protection and Personal Data Processing.
(a) Role allocation. Before processing any Personal Data, the Parties shall document and agree each Party's data-protection role (controller, processor, data intermediary, personal-information controller or processor, or equivalent under Applicable Law).
(b) Compliance. Each Party shall comply with all applicable data-protection laws in relation to its processing of Personal Data under this Agreement.
(c) Data Processing Agreement. Where the Counterparty processes Personal Data on behalf of the Company, the Parties shall enter into a Data Processing Agreement in the form set out in Schedule [●] (DPA) before any Personal Data is transferred or processed.
16.sellside:
Company as Processor. Where the Company receives Personal Data from the Counterparty, or processes Personal Data as a data intermediary or processor, the Company shall:
(a) process Personal Data only for the agreed purpose and on the Counterparty's instructions;
(b) implement security measures appropriate to the Personal Data processed; and
(c) subject to Applicable Law, assist the Counterparty with data-subject rights requests relating to Personal Data processed by the Company.
The Company's liability as processor is capped as set out in Clause [●] (Limitation of Liability), except for obligations that cannot be limited under applicable data-protection law.
16.fallback: Mutual Data-Protection Compliance (Low-Risk). Each Party shall comply with applicable data-protection laws in relation to any Personal Data it processes in connection with this Agreement.
16.counselNotes: Use the short mutual-compliance wording only for low-risk contracts not involving meaningful personal-data processing. Any contract involving systematic processing, sensitive data, cross-border transfer or customer data must use the full DPA framework (Baseline and Buy-Side).

17.title: Cross-Border Data Transfer
17.baseline:
Cross-Border Data Transfer. No Party may transfer Personal Data outside the originating jurisdiction except:
(a) in accordance with Applicable Law and this Agreement;
(b) using an approved transfer mechanism (adequacy decision, binding corporate rules, standard contractual clauses or equivalent approved by the relevant data-protection authority); and
(c) subject to the Company's prior written instructions or approval.
For the purposes of this Clause, "transfer" includes onward transfer by sub-processors and cloud service providers.
17.sellside: Company Transfers. Where the Company transfers Personal Data in connection with providing the Services, such transfers shall be: (a) disclosed in the Company's privacy policy or applicable customer-facing documentation; (b) subject to the safeguards required by Applicable Law; and (c) limited to the countries and recipients necessary to provide the Services.
17.fallback: Approved Sub-Processor List (Cloud / SaaS). For cloud or SaaS services using standard global infrastructure, transfers may be managed through an approved sub-processor list, provided that the Company receives: (a) at least [thirty (30)] days' advance notice of any new sub-processor; (b) a right to object within the notice period; and (c) a termination right if the new sub-processor is not approved and no alternative is available.
17.counselNotes: The approved sub-processor list suits standard cloud/SaaS infrastructure; for sensitive or regulated data, retain the Baseline and Buy-Side transfer controls.

18.title: Information Security and Cybersecurity
18.sellside: Company Security Limitation. The Company's security obligations are limited to those relating to its own systems and infrastructure as described in the Company's published security documentation. The Company is not responsible for security failures caused by the Counterparty's own systems, integrations, credentials, personnel or third-party services.
18.fallback: Industry-Standard Security (Low-Risk). The Counterparty shall implement industry-standard technical and organisational security measures appropriate to the Services and shall promptly notify the Company of any Security Incident.
18.counselNotes: Use the short industry-standard wording only for low-risk contracts not involving Personal Data, Customer Assets or production access; otherwise use the Baseline and Buy-Side security obligations.

19.title: Security Incident and Data Breach Notification
19.baseline:
Security Incident and Data Breach Notification. The Counterparty shall notify the Company without undue delay, and in any event within [twenty-four (24)] hours, after becoming aware of any actual or suspected Security Incident affecting the Company, Personal Data, Customer Assets, systems or the Services. The notification shall include:
(a) a description of the Security Incident, the systems or data affected and the likely impact;
(b) the measures taken or proposed to address it; and
(c) the contact details of the Counterparty's designated incident-response lead.
The Counterparty shall provide updates at regular intervals and shall support the Company in making any required regulatory, customer or third-party notifications.
19.sellside: Company Notification. The Company shall notify the Counterparty without undue delay of any Security Incident affecting the Counterparty's Personal Data processed by the Company, and shall cooperate in good faith with the Counterparty's investigation. The Company's notification obligations are subject to Applicable Law and shall not require it to disclose information that is legally privileged or would create security or enforcement risk.
19.fallback: 72-Hour Notification (Low-Risk). For contracts not involving Personal Data or Customer Assets, the Counterparty shall notify the Company of a Security Incident within [seventy-two (72)] hours, provided that: (a) the 72-hour period aligns with Applicable Law; and (b) the Company may require immediate notification where the incident is material, customer-facing or likely to trigger a regulatory notification.
19.counselNotes: Use the 72-hour trigger only for low-risk contracts with no Personal Data or Customer Assets; for data- or asset-sensitive contracts use the [twenty-four (24)]-hour Baseline/Buy-Side trigger.

20.title: Business Continuity, Disaster Recovery and Operational Resilience
20.sellside: Company Resilience Limitation. The Company's business-continuity and resilience obligations are limited to its own controlled systems. The Company is not responsible for the Counterparty's failure to implement adequate business continuity, or for failures caused by third-party infrastructure, cloud providers or force-majeure events outside the Company's control.
20.fallback: General BCP Obligation (Lower-Risk). The Counterparty shall maintain and test business-continuity procedures appropriate to the Services and provide evidence on request.
20.counselNotes: Use the general BCP obligation only for non-critical, lower-risk vendors; for critical or regulated services use the Baseline and Buy-Side resilience obligations.

21.title: Outsourcing, Subcontracting and Critical Third Parties
21.baseline: Outsourcing and Subcontracting. The Counterparty shall not subcontract any material obligation under this Agreement without the Company's prior written consent. The Counterparty remains fully responsible for the acts, omissions and defaults of its subcontractors as if they were its own, and shall flow down to each subcontractor all relevant obligations under this Agreement, including those relating to data protection, security, confidentiality, compliance and regulatory cooperation.
21.sellside: Company Subcontracting. The Company may subcontract performance of its obligations to its Affiliates or qualified third-party providers, provided that: (a) the Company remains responsible for performance; (b) the subcontractors are bound by confidentiality and data-protection obligations no less protective than this Agreement; and (c) the subcontracting does not alter the risk profile or regulatory status of the arrangement.
21.fallback: Notification and Objection (Non-Critical Subcontractors). For non-critical sub-processors and subcontractors, notification and objection rights apply in place of prior consent, provided that the subcontractor: (a) does not handle Personal Data, Customer Assets or production credentials; and (b) is subject to the Counterparty's existing data-protection and security obligations.
21.counselNotes: Notification-and-objection (rather than prior consent) is acceptable only for non-critical subcontractors meeting the conditions above; require prior written consent for any subcontractor handling Personal Data, Customer Assets, production access or regulated functions.

22.title: Cloud, SaaS, API, Platform and Technology Terms
22.baseline: Cloud, SaaS, API and Platform Terms. Access to any Platform, API, software, application or cloud service provided under this Agreement is: (a) limited to the Permitted Purpose, Permitted Users and usage limits set out in this Agreement; (b) subject to the Company's technical documentation, security requirements and acceptable-use policy; and (c) revocable immediately by the Company for breach of this Agreement or security risk. The Company retains all rights in its Platform, APIs, data and documentation.
22.sellside: Company Platform Use (Counterparty as User). The Counterparty's use of the Company's Platform or API is subject to: (a) the Company's acceptable-use policy and technical documentation; (b) the rate limits, usage caps and throttling specified; (c) a prohibition on scraping, reverse engineering, benchmarking or reselling the Company's data or platform; and (d) suspension by the Company for breach, excessive usage, security threat or prohibited use, without prior notice. No service-level commitment applies unless expressly agreed in writing.
22.counselNotes: Vendor standard terms may be accepted for standard SaaS contracts only after Legal/Security review and only where: (a) the data-processing terms align with the Company's DPA framework; (b) termination and data-export rights are expressly preserved; and (c) the liability and indemnity provisions meet the minimum thresholds approved by Legal.

23.title: Digital Assets, Gold, Custody, Wallet, Liquidity and Settlement
23.baseline: Digital Assets, Custody, Wallets, Liquidity and Settlement. Where the Services involve Customer Assets, Digital Assets, gold, custody, wallets, liquidity provision, exchange, payment, transfer, reconciliation or settlement infrastructure, the Counterparty shall comply with all applicable regulatory, operational, segregation, safeguarding, reconciliation, record-keeping and reporting requirements specified by the Company and required by Applicable Law.
23.sellside: Non-Custodial / Informational Services. Where the Company provides non-custodial or informational Services, the Company expressly does not: (a) hold, control, guarantee, underwrite, insure or safeguard Customer Assets; (b) provide investment, financial, trading, tax or custodial advice; or (c) take responsibility for counterparty default, settlement failure, exchange outage or market conditions. The Counterparty acknowledges this disclaimer and shall not represent the Company as a custodian, broker-dealer, settlement agent or guarantor.
23.counselNotes: Narrower asset provisions may be accepted only where: (a) there is no access to, control over, transfer of or settlement responsibility for Customer Assets; (b) the Company's role is solely informational or technology-provisioning; and (c) Legal and Compliance have confirmed that no custody, settlement or regulated-asset characterisation applies.

24.title: Intellectual Property Ownership
24.baseline: Intellectual Property Ownership. Each Party retains ownership of its pre-existing Intellectual Property Rights. Except as expressly stated in this Agreement, no right, title, interest or licence in either Party's Intellectual Property Rights is transferred or licensed by implication, estoppel, operation of law or otherwise.
24.buyside:
Ownership of Deliverables (Company).
(a) All Deliverables specifically created for the Company under this Agreement (including work product, reports, code, configurations, integrations, documentation, data models and analysis) shall be owned by the Company on creation as a work made for hire to the fullest extent permitted by law; where that characterisation is not available, the Counterparty hereby irrevocably assigns to the Company all rights in such Deliverables, including copyright, database rights, patent rights and all other Intellectual Property Rights. The Counterparty shall execute any documents required to perfect or record the assignment at the Company's request.
(b) Where the Counterparty incorporates its pre-existing Intellectual Property Rights into a Deliverable, the Counterparty grants the Company a worldwide, perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, non-exclusive licence to use that background IP to the extent necessary to use, maintain and exploit the Deliverable.
24.sellside: Company IP Retained. The Company retains all rights in its Platform, software, data, algorithms, models, documentation, feedback, roadmap, enhancements and derivative works. The Counterparty receives only the limited licence expressly granted in Clause [●] (Licence Rights) during the Term. Any feedback or suggestions provided by the Counterparty relating to the Company's Platform or Services shall be owned by the Company without restriction.
24.fallback: Licence in Lieu of Assignment. Where vendor ownership of bespoke Deliverables is commercially unavoidable, the Counterparty grants the Company a worldwide, perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, fully paid-up, non-exclusive licence to use, reproduce, modify, adapt, create derivative works from and sub-licence the Deliverables for the Company's internal and commercial purposes.
24.counselNotes: Accept a licence in lieu of assignment only where vendor ownership of bespoke Deliverables is commercially unavoidable; otherwise require assignment under the Buy-Side provision.

25.title: Licence Rights
25.baseline: Licence Rights. Any licence granted under this Agreement is: (a) limited to the Permitted Purpose and scope expressly stated; (b) non-exclusive, unless stated otherwise; (c) non-transferable and non-sublicensable without the Company's written consent; (d) revocable on the terms of this Agreement; and (e) subject to all stated terms, conditions and restrictions. No right, title or interest is conveyed except as expressly stated.
25.buyside: Licence to the Company. The Counterparty grants the Company a worldwide, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty-free licence to use the Deliverables and the Counterparty's background Intellectual Property Rights as embedded in the Deliverables, to the extent necessary for the Company to exploit, maintain, modify and sub-licence the Deliverables for its business purposes.
25.sellside: Licence to the Counterparty. The Company grants the Counterparty a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable, revocable licence to access and use the Company's Platform solely for the Permitted Purpose during the Term, subject to: (a) compliance with the Company's acceptable-use policy and technical documentation; (b) payment of all applicable Fees; and (c) immediate revocation on breach, termination or suspension. The Counterparty shall not sub-licence, resell, transfer or grant access to the Company's Platform to any third party without the Company's express written approval.
25.counselNotes: Accept a broader licence scope only where: (a) it is commercially priced and the risk has been specifically assessed; (b) it is limited to the Company's internal business purposes; and (c) it is no broader than necessary for the specific use case documented in the Statement of Work.

26.title: Work Product, Developments, Customisations and Feedback
26.baseline: Work Product, Developments and Feedback. All Deliverables specifically created for the Company under this Agreement shall be owned by the Company on creation or, if earlier, on full payment of the relevant Fees, as specified in the applicable Statement of Work. The Counterparty shall identify any background Intellectual Property Rights embedded in a Deliverable in the applicable Statement of Work.
26.buyside:
Enhanced Work-Product Obligations. The Counterparty shall:
(a) deliver all source code, assets, documentation and materials forming part of the Deliverables to the Company on acceptance;
(b) obtain and waive, to the extent permitted by law, any moral rights in the Deliverables on behalf of its personnel; and
(c) not use the Company's confidential requirements, designs, data models, specifications or product roadmap in deliverables for any other customer.
26.sellside: Feedback. All feedback, suggestions, ideas and improvements provided by the Counterparty relating to the Company's Platform, services or products are assigned to the Company without restriction. The Company may improve, commercialise or modify its Platform based on that feedback without obligation or payment to the Counterparty.
26.counselNotes: Accept vendor ownership of underlying tools or frameworks only where: (a) the Company receives a broad, irrevocable licence for the specific use case; (b) the tool or framework is identified as vendor IP in the Statement of Work; and (c) the tool is not specific to the Company and is available to the vendor's other customers.

27.title: Open-Source Software
27.baseline: Open-Source Software. The Counterparty shall not include open-source software in any Deliverable in a manner that would require: (a) the disclosure, licensing or transfer of the Company's proprietary source code, data or materials; (b) restrictions on the Company's ability to charge for the Deliverable or its derivatives; or (c) the application of any copyleft, share-alike or similar licence to the Company's proprietary materials.
27.sellside: Company-Supplied Open Source. Where the Company provides software or platform access containing open-source components, the Counterparty shall comply with all applicable open-source licence notices provided by the Company. The Counterparty shall not reverse engineer the Company's proprietary software or extract the Company's code from any delivered component.
27.counselNotes: Permissive open-source (e.g. MIT, Apache 2.0, BSD) may be accepted only if disclosed in the open-source inventory and confirmed not to contaminate the Company's proprietary code.

28.title: AI Tools and Automated Processing
28.baseline: AI Tools and Automated Processing. The Counterparty shall not use, input, upload, expose or make available the Company's Confidential Information, Personal Data, Customer Assets data, Intellectual Property Rights, content, materials or trade secrets to any artificial-intelligence tool, large language model, generative-AI system or machine-learning algorithm without the Company's prior written approval in each case.
28.sellside: Company AI Outputs. Where the Company provides AI-assisted or automated outputs as part of the Services, the Company disclaims liability for outcomes based on AI outputs that are: (a) used for legal, investment, tax, regulated or medical decision-making without independent professional review; or (b) inconsistent with the Counterparty's specific circumstances not disclosed to the Company. The Counterparty shall independently verify all AI-assisted outputs before relying on them.
28.counselNotes: Limited AI use may be accepted only if: (a) no Personal Data or Confidential Information is processed by the AI tool; (b) all outputs are human-reviewed before use; and (c) the AI tool is identified and approved by the Company in writing.

29.title: Confidentiality
29.baseline:
Confidentiality.
(a) Each Party shall: (i) keep all Confidential Information received from the other Party strictly confidential; (ii) use it only for the purposes of this Agreement; and (iii) disclose it only to its officers, employees, directors, advisers and subcontractors who need to know and who are bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than this Clause.
(b) Each Party shall notify the other immediately on becoming aware of any breach of this Clause.
(c) This Clause survives termination of this Agreement indefinitely for trade secrets and for [five (5)] years for other Confidential Information, unless the Parties agree otherwise.
29.sellside: Company Confidentiality Limitation. The Company's confidentiality obligations are limited to information clearly marked as confidential, or which a reasonable party would understand to be confidential given the context. The Company may disclose Confidential Information to its Affiliates, advisers, Regulators, legal counsel, auditors and service providers on a need-to-know basis without consent, subject to appropriate confidentiality obligations.
29.fallback: Fixed Survival Period. This Clause survives termination for [three (3)] years in respect of ordinary business Confidential Information; trade secrets, security information, customer data and Personal Data remain protected indefinitely.
29.counselNotes: A fixed [three (3)]-year survival period is acceptable for ordinary business information, but trade secrets, security information, customer data and Personal Data must remain protected indefinitely.

30.title: Publicity, Announcements, Trademarks and Marketing References
30.baseline: Publicity, Announcements and Trademarks. Neither Party may issue any press release, public announcement, marketing material, social-media post, website content or investor communication that uses the other Party's name, logo, trademark, trade name, brand, products or relationship without prior written approval, except as required by law. Where disclosure is required by law, the disclosing Party shall give the other as much advance notice as reasonably practicable.
30.sellside: Company Marketing References. The Company may identify the Counterparty as a customer or partner in the Company's factual marketing materials where commercially appropriate, subject to this Agreement. The Counterparty may not use the Company's brand or name in any context that could imply the Company's endorsement, warranty or regulatory status.
30.fallback: Approved Announcement. A Party may issue a single public announcement of the relationship using text approved in advance in writing by the other Party's Legal and Communications functions, provided that no regulatory status, endorsement or investment claim is made.
